## Q2

Consider $$
A =
\begin{bmatrix}
2 & 0 & 1 \\
0 & 3 & -1 \\
1 & -1 & 4
\end{bmatrix},
\qquad
B =
\begin{bmatrix}
1 & 2 & 0\\
2 & 5 & -3 \\
0 & -3 & 6
\end{bmatrix}.
$$

a.  State the dimensions of $A$ and identify $a_{23}$. \[2 Marks\]

::: callout-tip
Your answer here
:::

```{r}
A <- matrix(c(2,0,1,0,3,-1,1,-1,4), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE)
dim(A)
A[2,3]
```

b.  Is $A$ a square matrix? Is it symmetric? Justify your answer using
    the definition $A=A^\top$, not just by inspection. \[2 Marks\]

::: callout-tip
A is a square Matrix because the row and columns are the same size A is
Symmetric when it equals its on transpose. In this case A is symmetric.

$$ 
A = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\0 & 3 & -1 \\1 & -1 & 4\end{bmatrix},
A^T = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 1 \\0 & 3 & -1 \\1 & -1 & 4\end{bmatrix}
$$

```{r}
dim(A)
```
:::

c.  Is $A$ a diagonal matrix? Explain why or why not. \[1 Mark\]

::: callout-tip
A is not a diagonal matrix. A diagonal matrix only has non-zero values
along its main diagonal and zero in all elements not in the diagonal.
This matrix has non-zero values in the elements that do not lie in the
main diagonal
:::

d.  In R, Enter $A$ and $B$ into R. Use `isSymmetric()` to confirm your
    answer to part (b) for both matrices. \[4 Marks\]

::: callout-tip
Your answer here
:::
